summary: npm wrapper ships and launches opaque 34MB Windows PE with no legitimate function
details: The package's only shipped code is a thin launcher around a bundled 34MB Windows executable at assets/Helper.exe (sha256 e5a585e03e1725d5030fd4854805933d53aa86cfbbb0b3808dffcc63782ddf38). index.js calls spawn(BUNDLED_EXE, [], { detached: true, stdio: "ignore" }) to launch the binary detached with no output capture. A shipped postinstall.js performs the same detached launch of assets/Helper.exe on win32, and the README states "The postinstall script starts the executable." The published package.json sets scripts to an empty object, so npm does not invoke postinstall.js automatically for this specific version — the binary runs when the user invokes the package's exported launcher, or if a subsequent version restores the hook. The binary itself is opaque: no source is shipped, no documented function is given, no hash or signature is published, and it imports BCrypt decryption APIs together with CreateProcess, CopyFile, and VirtualProtect while reading USERNAME and USERDOMAIN — a packed-executable shape consistent with a loader/dropper rather than a declared utility. The package name, the "Helper.exe" / "runHello" naming, and the absence of any described feature constitute a cover story around opaque Windows code execution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
